sentences.text: Limenavis belongs to the ornithuran dinosaurs, a group of Late Cretaceous reptiles closely related to birds.
This genus includes Limenavis patagonica, a species viewed as one of the stem-bird species nearest to the common ancestor of all modern birds.
The name Limenavis means 'bird of the threshold' or 'limit-bird', derived from Latin words for threshold and bird.
The specific name patagonica reflects the location where the fossil was unearthed in Patagonia.
The genus Limenavis was formally named by Clarke and Chiappe in 2001.
The single known species, Limenavis patagonica, was found in the lower member of the Allen Formation at Salitral Moreno, 20 km south of General Roca in Río Negro, Argentina.
The parent group of Limenavis is Ornithurae.
Early analyses by Clarke and Chiappe placed Limenavis in Carinatae, suggesting it was more advanced than Ichthyornis but not part of the modern bird group Neornithes.
However, a 2013 study by O'Connor and colleagues proposed that Limenavis is slightly more primitive than Ichthyornis.
Limenavis lived approximately 70 million years ago at the Campanian-Maastrichtian boundary of the Late Cretaceous.
Its time range falls within the Maastrichtian stage, spanning between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
